user_input: remove Django backend and with same funtionality and frontend; clarified: target is Django/Python and remove Laravel completely
title: Laravel to Django backend replacement

assessment_snapshot.intro: The workspace contains a Next.js frontend and a Laravel/PHP API, not an existing Django backend. The migration plan found:
bullets: 58 API routes, 22 model files, and 34 migration-defined tables
Frontend points to the local API at 127.0.0.1:8000
User requested Django/Python, feature parity and removal of Laravel; Socket.IO service is separate

proposed_outcome: Replace the Laravel backend in place with a Django API while preserving the frontend and its user-facing behavior, keeping API contracts compatible where possible, migrating existing SQLite data and required settings, then removing Laravel source files without exposing secrets.

questions.title: Django version
questions.question: Which Django version and API framework should the replacement use?

options.label: Django 5.2 LTS + Django REST Framework
Django 6.x + Django REST Framework

questions.title: API compatibility
questions.question: How strictly should the Django API preserve the current Laravel endpoints and responses?
questions.prefilled_value: must preserve; keep the existing frontend working

options.label: Must preserve routes, payloads, and status-code behavior for the existing frontend
Breaking changes are allowed if versioned
A redesigned API is allowed

questions.title: SQLite data migration
questions.question: How should the current SQLite data be moved into the Django backend?
questions.prefilled_value: Migrate existing SQLite data; active database path/schema should be identified locally

options.label: Create Django-owned schema and migrate/transform existing SQLite data into it
Keep the same SQLite database and adapt Django to its existing schema
Assess the active database and schema first, then choose the safest migration

questions.title: Authentication migration
questions.question: What should happen to existing Laravel Sanctum users and bearer tokens?
questions.recommended: preserve users and compatible tokens where feasible; require sign-in again if needed
questions.default: preserve existing auth mechanism; detect from codebase

options.value: preserve users and compatible tokens where feasible; require sign-in again if needed
options.label: Migrate users and preserve compatible tokens where feasible; require sign-in again if a token cannot be safely retained

options.value: migrate users; invalidate tokens and require sign-in
options.label: Migrate user accounts but invalidate all existing tokens

options.value: replace auth with JWT; require sign-in
options.label: Move to JWT authentication and require sign-in

questions.title: Performance expectations
questions.question: What response-time or availability target should Django meet?
questions.recommended: match current production baseline; no regression
questions.default: match current production baseline; no regression

options.value: match current production baseline; no regression
options.label: Match the current baseline; no regression
p95 latency under 200 ms
Specify another target

questions.title: Definition of done
questions.question: What outcomes define a successful migration?
questions.recommended: feature parity verified by tests and smoke checks
questions.default: feature parity with the current system; all existing user-facing behaviors preserved
questions.prefilled_value: same functionality and frontend; feature parity

options.value: feature parity with current system; all existing user-facing behaviors preserved
options.label: Feature parity; all existing user-facing behaviors preserved

options.value: feature parity verified by tests and smoke checks
options.label: Feature parity verified by automated tests and smoke checks

questions.title: Out-of-scope components
questions.question: Which existing components should not be changed as part of this backend migration?
questions.default: no explicit exclusions; agent will infer from project structure
questions.prefilled_value: Do not redesign the Next.js frontend or change the separate Socket.IO service except for essential API integration compatibility.

questions.title: Test policy
questions.question: How should the existing test suites be handled during migration?
questions.recommended: partial: preserve frontend tests and add Django API parity tests

options.label: Existing tests must pass; add Django tests for migrated behavior
Rewrite tests with equivalent Django coverage

options.value: partial: preserve frontend tests and add Django API parity tests
options.label: Preserve frontend tests and add equivalent Django API tests; replace Laravel-specific tests

questions.title: Replacement location
questions.question: Where should the Django backend be created?
questions.prefilled_value: in-place; replace Laravel while keeping frontend/ and socket-server/

options.label: Replace Laravel inside the existing backend/ directory
Create backend-django-new beside the existing backend/ first

questions.title: Additional constraints
questions.question: Add any additional migration constraints, or leave the stated constraints unchanged.
questions.default: None beyond the decisions listed in this specification.
questions.prefilled_value: Preserve all existing user-facing features and the current frontend. Migrate SQLite data and required settings before deleting Laravel files. Do not reveal secrets.
